name: _sparse_mm
description: Representative ATen signature (not an exclusive ABI): aten::_sparse_mm(Tensor sparse, Tensor dense) -> Tensor. This representative overload is not exclusive: the original Gems pytest defines the full contract for this operator, and its calls, keyword arguments, returns, errors, aliasing and mutation behavior must not be narrowed to this one signature. All supplied registered schemas, verbatim: aten::_sparse_mm(Tensor sparse, Tensor dense) -> Tensor ; aten::_sparse_mm.reduce(Tensor sparse, Tensor dense, str reduce) -> Tensor. Semantics: sparse matrix multiplication of a sparse left operand by a dense right operand, yielding a dense Tensor of shape (rows, cols). The sparse operand may be COO (coalesced or not, with implicit coalescing of duplicate/unsorted coordinates, stored zeros, empty supports, nonzero storage offsets, zero extents) or CSR, and may also be paired with a second sparse operand (COO x COO, CSR x CSR) or with a dense left operand, which the operator accepts natively through its addmm fallback; the outcome for those forms is defined by the tests, not by this representative signature. Additional parameters: the registered reduce overload takes a trailing str reduce argument (semantic values such as 'sum', 'mean', 'amax', 'amin'), which pytest covers as a vendor-scoped negative; that overload and the argument are outside this representative signature but remain part of the original contract. Failure modes are the tests' business and are not expressed here: pytest maps operands below rank 2 to IndexError, rank-3 operands and the inner-dimension mismatch to RuntimeError, the shape mismatch to RuntimeError or ValueError, and non-tensor operands and dtype mismatch to RuntimeError or TypeError, with the unsupported-dtype negative created only for the measured vendor.
